_about: Owner rulings of 5 Oct 2026 (GRADER-CORE-1 spec WHY, rulings (2)-(7)) applied to the examiner-verified expectations (data/verify/items.verified.json + data/supplement/items.supplement.json). The loader (lib/data.cjs applyRepins) applies each row ONLY if the current value still equals `old`, and throws otherwise, so a later edit to the verified set cannot be silently overwritten. Rows with `kind: settled` change no value: the ruling settles a contest the audit left open in favour of the verified value, so `contested` becomes false. Rows with `kind: added` add a field the verified set did not carry (v2-only fields are scored only on responses produced with acceptsV2). Cases the rulings do not settle keep their verified value and are listed under `unsettled`.

rulings.2: A miscopied value is penalised ONCE (silly); the work after it earns ECF marks.
rulings.3: A wrongly formed equation then solved correctly loses the forming marks and earns the solving marks (ECF). 'Departure = zero' is kept ONLY for answering a different problem or using an invalid method.
rulings.4: Crossed-out / withdrawn work is not assessed.
rulings.5: No deduction for missing state symbols.
rulings.6: Maths units follow the question's scheme; a silent scheme means no deduction. Science keeps unit deductions.
rulings.7: Mistake type: copied wrongly = silly, performed wrongly = calculation, method misunderstood = conceptual, CBSE format only = presentation, unattempted = no type.
rulings.A17-1: A17 owner ruling (GRADING-JOBS-1, 2026-10-06): a missing or wrong unit on the FINAL answer of a quantity-valued answer costs exactly ½ in Maths AND Science, at most ½ per question, typed presentation; never on a pure number. SUPERSEDES ruling 6's Maths half.
rulings.A17-3: A17 owner ruling 3 AS CHANGED BY THE OWNER 2026-10-06 (supersedes the spec text "Hinglish never deducted"): CBSE answers are in English or in Hindi in Devanagari; an answer written in Hinglish (Roman-script Hindi mixed with English) keeps its content marks and loses exactly 1/2 once per answer, typed presentation (exam technique), comment "Write in English (or Hindi in Devanagari): board examiners expect one medium." English with technical terms and Devanagari Hindi are never penalised; no other language deduction.

repins.basis: The times are reversed (480/x - 480/(x-8) = 3): a wrongly FORMED equation for the same problem, not a different problem and not an invalid method. The forming marks (step 2, 1.5) are lost; x^2 - 8x + 1280 = 0 is correctly derived from the student's own equation and earns the solving mark (step 3, 1.5, ECF). Steps 4-5 stay 0 because (x - 40)(x + 32) is not a factorisation of the student's quadratic (fudged), so the final 40 km/h is not 'solved correctly'. This equals the CBSE-instruction-10 alternative the verifier recorded (2/5).
ECF on the solving step (see the totalMarks row).
Not a departure under ruling 3: same problem, valid method, wrong equation formed.
A departure flag is no longer required (or correct) here; the grader should charge the forming step once and carry the error forward.
Ruling 3 settles the marks contest in favour of the CBSE ECF view.
Miscopied PR = 9 for 6: penalised once (silly), ECF on the rest. Verified value 1.5/2 silly stands; the app's miscopy-as-departure view (0/2) is overruled.
u copied as -90 for -60: penalised once (silly), v = -22.5 cm earns ECF. Verified value 1.5/2 silly stands; the app view (0.5/2) is overruled.
The P = V/I lines are explicitly withdrawn by the student and are not assessed: 4/4, no mistake type, nothing for Mistake Intelligence. App case law 2 (3.5/4) is overruled.

3x - 2 = 0 solved as x = 3/2 from correct factors: the solving step was PERFORMED wrongly (nothing was copied) = calculation. Verified value stands; the app's worked example calling this 'silly' is overruled.
The sign is lost while REWRITING (cos t - sin t) as (sin t - cos t) inside the student's own algebra: an operation performed wrongly = calculation, not a value copied wrongly. Verified value stands.

Controller decision D33 (2026-10-05), replacing the PR-1 builder-judgement re-pin (mistakeType null / unattempted): the student ATTEMPTED the question — correct skeletal equations for both reactions — so it is not unattempted (ruling 7's fourth state is for work not attempted). Balancing was not attempted where the question asks for it, which is the restored S4a rule: an equation left UNBALANCED when a balanced equation was asked for = conceptual (attempted balancing with wrong coefficients would be calculation, S4b). The verified value (conceptual, wrong step 2) stands; marks unchanged (1/2).
A calculator decimal 'proof' of irrationality is an invalid method: departure = zero is kept (0/3).
HCF(85, 72) is computed instead of HCF(84, 70): a different problem, departure = zero is kept (0/2).

The wrong nth-term formula a + nd is RE-APPLIED in (ii) (a wrong method, not a carried wrong value), so (i)-(ii) earn 0; the student returns at (iii) and earns normally: 2/4 unchanged. Contrast owner-anomaly-01 Q4, where a wrong value is carried into correct methods and earns ECF.
Part (ii) is unattempted: a fourth state with no type (scored only on acceptsV2 responses, which carry step status 'unattempted').
Part (iii)(a) 'I don't know' is unattempted: a fourth state with no type.
The verification is unattempted: a fourth state with no type.
A blank page: both parts unattempted (an honest decline is also accepted, as before).

unsettled.why: The balanced equation was asked for and written unbalanced while (c)(i) balances correctly: not 'copied wrongly', arguably not 'method misunderstood', and not an unattempted sub-task (the equation was written). The rulings do not decide between conceptual and a slip; the verified value is kept.
'clotting cells' for 'platelets': whether a missing CBSE technical term is 'CBSE format only' (presentation) or a knowledge gap (conceptual) is not decided by the rulings; the verified value is kept.
Not contested on marks: the official MS 2025 Q35 erratum (class width 3 vs 2) has no defensible alternative; the golden set follows the correct mathematics.
